'''''Allium trifoliatum''''', commonly called '''pink garlic''' or '''hirsute garlic''', is a [[Mediterranean]] species of [[Allium|wild onion]]. It is native to [[France]], [[Cyprus]], [[Malta]], [[Italy]] ([[Sicily]], [[Sardinia]], [[Calabria]], [[Basilicata]], [[Apulia]], [[Campania]], [[Abruzzo]]), [[Greece]], [[Egypt]], [[Turkey]], [[Lebanon]],  [[Palestine]], and [[Israel]].<ref name=charlene>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=296831 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref><ref>[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=allium+trifoliatum Altervista Flora Italiana, Aglio a tre foglie, ''Allium trifoliatum'']</ref><ref>Kollmann, Fania Weissmann. 1976. Israel Journal of Botany. Jerusalem 24(4): 204, <big>שום שעיר</big> ''Allium trifoliatum'' subsp. ''hirsutum''  and ''Allium trifoliatum'' var. ''sterile''</ref><ref>Meikle, R.D. (1985). Flora of Cyprus 2: 833-1970. The Bentham-Moxon Trust Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew.</ref><ref>Danin, A. (2004). Distribution Atlas of Plants in the Flora Palaestina area: 1-517. The Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities, Jerusalem.</ref><ref>Dobignard, D. & Chatelain, C. (2010). Index synonymique de la flore d'Afrique du nord 1: 1-455. Éditions des conservatoire et jardin botaniques, Genève.</ref>

''Allium trifoliatum'' is a perennial herb up to 30 cm tall. It has a tight [[umbel]] with short [[Pedicel (botany)|pedicels]]. [[Tepals]] are white, sometimes with pink to red midveins.<ref>Domenico Maria Leone Cirillo. 1792. Plantarum Rariorum Regni Neapolitani. Napoli  Fasc. ii. 11.</ref><ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20140329193418/http://www.rareplants.co.uk/product.asp?P_ID=3667&strPageHistory=related|title=Rare Plants UK, ''Allium trifoliatum''}}</ref>
